title: OGL game
description: One open-source game in the OGL catalog. Maintainers add a game by committing a file like this under catalog/games on the catalog branch. Players do not add games. OGL reads the folder at launch, then finds versions from each channel's GitHub releases. A game either lists channels and platforms to install, or a web address to play in its own window, or both.

$schema.description: Editor hint. Point game files at ../game.schema.json.

id.description: Stable id used for install folders. Never rename it after a release.

mark.description: One to three letters drawn on the library tile. Defaults to the start of the name.

website.description: Project site. Opened in the browser.

note.description: Optional requirement, such as needing the original game files.

cover.description: Wide https image used as the banner and store card, ideally 16:9 and at least 1280 wide. Without it OGL uses the website's og:image, then the first screenshot.

icon.description: Square https image used in the sidebar and on the game page. Without it OGL uses the website's apple-touch-icon, then the GitHub owner's avatar.

screenshots.description: In-game screenshots shown on the game page.

tags.description: Genres shown as search filters, such as Strategy or City builder.

url.description: Page that runs the game. OGL opens it in its own window with its own saved data.

web.description: Play in a window instead of installing. Use for browser games. Such games show on every system.

name.description: The original game, such as RollerCoaster Tycoon 2.

url.description: Where to get it, such as its GOG page.

requires.description: The original game whose files this project needs. Shown as a Needs tag that links to the store, and as a filter on Home.

channels.description: Where versions come from. Each channel is a GitHub releases list. A new release appears in OGL without a new OGL build.

platforms.description: Which operating systems this game publishes, and how to recognize and launch the file. A player only sees games that list their system.

label.description: Track label, such as Release or Develop.

description.description: One line under the track picker, such as how stable the builds are.

type.description: Read versions from GitHub releases at runtime.

prerelease.description: exclude hides pre-releases, only keeps them, include keeps both.

cdn.description: Read version numbers from GitHub releases but files from this CDN, for projects that do not attach files to releases. openttd reads cdn.openttd.org manifests.

oneOf.description: A download page that lists the project's files, one per table row, such as a web server's folder listing. OGL takes each version from the file name. The host must be one OGL already downloads from (src/shared/urls.ts).

prerelease.description: A file name with alpha, beta or rc after the version counts as a pre-release.

oneOf.description: A free itch.io game page. OGL reads the uploads listed on the page and takes the version from the file name, so there is one version at a time.

archive.description: zip, tar.gz and tar.xz are extracted. dmg is a macOS disk image; OGL copies the .app bundles out of it. file is launched as the download itself, which covers AppImage and other single-file builds.

assetRule.description: Pick one release asset for this machine by case-insensitive filename fragments. Arch tokens prefer the longer match, so x86_64 does not count as x86.

include.description: The filename must contain one of these. Use windows, macos, or linux.

exclude.description: Drop symbol packages, installers, checksums, and debug files.

prefer.description: Break ties. portable or appimage are typical.

arch.description: Tokens for each CPU. List universal under every arch it should fit. Omit arch only when every matching file runs everywhere.

app.description: macOS bundle name to open, such as OpenRCT2.app. A file name, not a path.

binary.description: Executable file name inside the archive, such as openrct2.exe. A * matches any text, for names that carry a version.

env.description: Environment variables passed to the game executable.

runtime.description: An engine the game file runs inside, downloaded once from a GitHub release and shared between games. OGL starts the engine with the game's launch file as its argument. LÖVE for .love games is the typical case.
